discovery_and_framing.subtitle: Master discovery and framing before building any GTM plan

lesson.hook: Stop pitching solutions before you even know what winning looks like.
lesson.what: Discovery and framing means establishing clear goals, hard constraints, and success definitions before proposing any launch strategies. It prevents you from solving the wrong problem with an unfocused plan.
how: Define a specific numerical target for the first ninety days.
Identify your primary operational or financial constraint immediately.
Establish clear metrics that separate success from failure early on.
lesson.example: For launching Spotify HiFi, state a clear goal of ten percent conversion within twelve months while keeping churn below two percent.
lesson.mistake: Jumping straight into marketing channels and tactics without defining a single concrete success metric.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch a premium subscription tier for Spotify?
questions.scenario: You are starting the Spotify HiFi interview case and need to set the right tone.
questions.question: What is the best way to open your discovery and framing phase?
options: State a clear twelve month conversion goal and churn limit.
Analyze competitor pricing strategies across the entire streaming industry.
Propose building social features to drive massive viral acquisition loops.
Design a complex multi channel marketing campaign across global regions.
questions.explanation: Setting a precise conversion target and churn limit establishes immediate strategic alignment. Vague ambitions or premature channel tactics fail to frame the core challenge.
whyWrong: Analyzing competitor pricing feels thorough, but framing requires setting your own goals before evaluating market rates.
A smart candidate might suggest viral loops to drive scale, but that ignores the need for foundational conversion goals.
Designing a multi channel campaign sounds proactive, but it skips the essential step of defining success metrics first.

questions.caseTitle: Strategy for a US fintech app entering the European market.
questions.scenario: Your US fintech app is planning an ambitious expansion across Europe.
questions.question: How should you frame this market entry to avoid a messy rollout?
options: Partner with every major European bank before writing any code.
Aim for a profitable beachhead in one specific market first.
Translate the entire product interface into twenty different local languages.
Launch simultaneous marketing blitzes across all major European capitals.
questions.explanation: Focusing on a single profitable market prevents resource dilution during international expansion. Trying to conquer the whole continent at once guarantees operational failure.
whyWrong: Partnering with every bank sounds secure, but it creates massive blockers before you even test market demand.
Translating every interface feels user centric, but framing requires prioritizing one beachhead market before scaling localization.
A smart candidate might argue for a continental blitz to maximize reach, but that ignores severe resource constraints.

questions.caseTitle: Design a launch plan for a D2C brand entering a new market.
questions.scenario: You are introducing a direct to consumer cashmere brand to the British market.
questions.question: Which framing approach establishes the most effective baseline for success?
options: Target one million pounds in net revenue within ninety days.
Reduce product prices by half to undercut all existing local competitors.
Build a massive warehouse network to support nationwide same day shipping.
Sponsor twenty major celebrity influencers to create instant brand awareness.
questions.explanation: A specific revenue target paired with a timeframe gives the launch clear accountability. Operational scaling or discounting without goals leads to margin destruction.
whyWrong: Reducing prices might drive initial volume, but it destroys unit economics without a clear framing strategy.
A smart candidate might focus on infrastructure to ensure fulfillment, but supply chain setup should follow financial framing.
Sponsoring celebrity influencers seems like a fast growth hack, but it bypasses crucial revenue and acquisition cost constraints.

questions.caseTitle: Plan the launch of a B2B SaaS product for small businesses.
questions.scenario: Your team built a new B2B SaaS product for small retail shop owners.
questions.question: How should you frame the target customer segment during discovery?
options: Build custom integrations for every possible third party software vendor.
Market broadly to any small business needing basic administrative tools.
Target large enterprise retail chains with dedicated procurement departments.
Focus tightly on owner operated retail shops with zero IT staff.
questions.explanation: Narrowing the audience to retail shops with no IT staff defines a precise, reachable beachhead. Broad targeting leads to diluted messaging and bloated product requirements.
whyWrong: Building custom integrations sounds helpful for sales, but it expands scope before validating core product demand.
Marketing broadly feels inclusive, but lack of focus prevents you from solving specific workflow pain points.
A smart candidate might chase enterprise revenue for higher ACV, but the case specifically targets resource constrained small businesses.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch Amazon's same-day delivery in a new city?
questions.scenario: Amazon is bringing same day delivery to a major new metropolitan area.
questions.question: What primary constraint must you acknowledge upfront in your framing?
options: Driver network density during the critical first month of operations.
Consumer preference for standard two day shipping over speed.
Total number of warehouses required to cover the entire continent.
Regulatory approvals needed for drone delivery in rural sectors.
questions.explanation: Driver network density directly dictates whether same day delivery can actually succeed locally. Other constraints are either irrelevant to this specific launch or prematurely broad.
whyWrong: Consumer preference matters, but operational capacity is the primary constraint when launching physical fulfillment.
A smart candidate might think about continent wide logistics, but a city launch depends entirely on local driver density.
Regulatory approvals for drones are fascinating, but same day delivery relies on ground vehicles and local hubs.

questions.caseTitle: Design the GTM for Meta's WhatsApp Business API in Europe.
questions.scenario: You are leading the European launch of the WhatsApp Business API for merchants.
questions.question: How should you define success for this enterprise and merchant rollout?
options: Reach one hundred thousand active accounts retaining above sixty percent.
Achieve complete market saturation across every single European business sector.
Eliminate all traditional email marketing channels across the European Union.
Generate immediate billion dollar revenue through high upfront software licensing.
questions.explanation: Combining active account acquisition with a retention threshold creates a realistic success definition. Unrealistic saturation goals ignore natural market friction and churn.
whyWrong: A smart candidate might aim for total market saturation, but setting unmeasured universal goals invites execution failure.
Eliminating email is an extreme vision that distracts from the core goal of merchant adoption and retention.
Generating billion dollar revenue sounds ambitious, but API monetization usually scales through transaction volume over time.

questions.caseTitle: Global Streaming Service Expansion
questions.scenario: Your streaming platform is preparing to launch in a brand new developing market.
questions.question: What is the most critical first step in your discovery and framing?
options: Design a multi tiered pricing structure with five distinct subscription plans.
Build proprietary studio infrastructure to produce local original content.
Establish local bandwidth constraints and dominant mobile device tiers.
Secure exclusive global rights to Hollywood blockbuster movie franchises.
questions.explanation: Understanding local technical constraints like bandwidth and device tiers is essential for a viable launch plan. Content licensing or pricing tiers mean nothing if the app cannot stream smoothly.
whyWrong: Designing complex pricing tiers feels strategic, but you must understand local purchasing power and tech specs first.
Building production studios is a long term play that ignores immediate market entry constraints.
A smart candidate might prioritize Hollywood content for appeal, but local technical constraints dictate if users can even stream.

questions.caseTitle: Enterprise Cybersecurity Platform Launch
questions.scenario: You are introducing a new cloud security posture management tool to enterprises.
questions.question: How should you frame the initial go to market objective for the board?
options: Run television advertisements during major tech conferences globally.
Acquire one million free trial users within the first thirty days.
Open office locations in ten major financial capitals simultaneously.
Secure fifty design partners with multi million dollar annual contracts.
questions.explanation: Enterprise cybersecurity relies on high value design partners who validate the product and provide crucial feedback. Consumer volume metrics or flashy ads are completely misaligned with B2B enterprise sales.
whyWrong: Running television ads sounds like a great brand awareness play, but enterprise buyers do not purchase security software that way.
A smart candidate might suggest a million free users for bottom up growth, but enterprise security requires high touch validation.
Opening global offices prematurely burns capital before you have validated product market fit with core design partners.

target_segment.subtitle: Master the art of picking the exact beachhead customer segment.

lesson.hook: If you try to sell your product to everyone, you will sell it to no one.
lesson.what: Targeting is about choosing a specific group of people with an urgent problem. A beachhead segment gives you the fastest path to initial traction and product market fit.
how: Find users experiencing high pain right now
Look for groups who are easy to reach
Avoid markets requiring massive upfront education
lesson.example: For Spotify HiFi, we targeted audiophiles already paying for premium who desperately want lossless audio quality.
lesson.mistake: Picking a massive demographic like millennials instead of a narrow, high-intent user group.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch a premium subscription tier for Spotify?
questions.scenario: Spotify wants to introduce an ultra-high-fidelity streaming tier for music enthusiasts.
questions.question: Which target segment represents the best beachhead for this launch?
options: Hardcore audiophiles and high income households
Casual listeners using free mobile ad tiers
Older adults who listen to audiobooks daily
Teenagers sharing family plans across devices
questions.explanation: Hardcore audiophiles already care deeply about sound quality and have the disposable income to pay more. This group provides the highest conversion probability for a premium tier.
whyWrong: Casual free tier listeners are unlikely to upgrade immediately without experiencing sound quality limits.
Older audiobook listeners have different engagement patterns than music focused audiophiles.
Teenagers on family plans typically lack the budget for standalone higher priced tiers.

questions.caseTitle: Strategy for a US fintech app entering the European market.
questions.scenario: A growing American consumer finance application is preparing its expansion into Europe.
questions.question: What is the optimal target segment and market entry wedge?
options: Every smartphone owner in Western Europe
British users in the highest income brackets
Continental Europe digital nomads across nations
The UK market due to language and adoption
questions.explanation: Selecting the UK market provides a concentrated English speaking population with high fintech adoption. This avoids the fragmentation of a continental spray strategy.
whyWrong: Targeting every smartphone owner violates the core rule of focusing on a specific beachhead.
Focusing only on high income brackets is too narrow for a broad fintech application launch.
Continental digital nomads are too dispersed to build initial market density efficiently.

questions.caseTitle: Design a launch plan for a D2C brand entering a new market.
questions.scenario: Quince is launching its affordable luxury cashmere and basics brand in the United Kingdom.
questions.question: Which initial customer segment should the brand prioritize for maximum early traction?
options: Traditional department store shoppers in rural towns
Affluent urban professionals valuing quiet luxury basics
Teenagers shopping exclusively on social media apps
Bargain hunters looking for fast fashion discounts
questions.explanation: Affluent urban professionals appreciate high quality cashmere and luxury basics at accessible price points. They represent the exact demographic for the Quince value proposition.
whyWrong: Traditional department store shoppers in rural towns have different purchasing habits and preferences.
Teenagers shopping on social media typically buy trendy fast fashion rather than basics.
Bargain hunters may reject luxury pricing despite affordability compared to traditional brands.

questions.caseTitle: Plan the launch of a B2B SaaS product for small businesses.
questions.scenario: A new software tool designed to streamline small business operations is ready for launch.
questions.question: Who should be the primary beachhead segment for this software?
options: Owner operated retail shops with zero IT staff
Freelance consultants working from home offices
Large retail chains with dedicated IT departments
Mid market companies scaling their HR departments
questions.explanation: Owner operated retail shops with no IT staff experience acute operational pain that simple software can solve. They make decisions quickly without complex enterprise procurement cycles.
whyWrong: Freelance consultants have lower software budgets and different daily operational workflows.
Large retail chains require enterprise features and lengthy sales cycles, not small business SaaS.
Mid market companies hiring HR staff operate at a scale beyond simple small business tools.

questions.caseTitle: How would Microsoft Teams enter the education market against Google Classroom?
questions.scenario: Microsoft Teams needs to find a profitable entry point into the education sector.
questions.question: Which educational segment offers the best wedge against entrenched competitors?
options: K12 school districts with zero software budget
After school tutoring centers and music academies
Primary and secondary schools using free Gmail
Higher education institutions needing research security
questions.explanation: Google Classroom dominates primary schools with free tools, but higher education demands complex research collaboration and enterprise security. Universities provide a strong wedge where Microsoft excels.
whyWrong: K12 districts with zero budget cannot afford paid enterprise software licenses.
After school tutoring centers are too small and fragmented to drive institutional adoption.
Primary and secondary schools are already locked into Google Classroom ecosystems.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Shopify's point-of-sale system to small retailers.
questions.scenario: Shopify is expanding its hardware point of sale system to physical merchants.
questions.question: What is the most effective target segment for this hardware launch?
options: Entirely offline mom and pop retail stores
High volume restaurants needing table management
Existing online Shopify merchants running pop ups
Large department stores switching legacy registers
questions.explanation: Online merchants already using Shopify for their digital catalogs are the ideal wedge. They already trust the platform and occasionally sell offline at weekend pop ups.
whyWrong: Offline mom and pop stores require extensive education and high customer acquisition costs.
High volume restaurants need specialized hospitality features rather than general retail point of sale.
Large department stores require complex custom integrations beyond standard retail hardware.

questions.caseTitle: Bonus: Launching Spotify Car Thing hardware device
questions.scenario: Spotify is introducing a dedicated hardware accessory for playing music inside older cars.
questions.question: Which target segment should be prioritized for this device launch?
options: Cyclists and runners working out at the gym
Audiophiles building high end home stereo systems
Commuters driving older vehicles without modern touchscreens
Luxury car owners with built in premium dashboards
questions.explanation: Drivers of older vehicles lack modern smart dashboards and struggle with phone controls while driving. This specific group experiences the exact physical pain point the hardware solves.
whyWrong: Cyclists and runners cannot use a car accessory during their physical fitness workouts.
Audiophiles at home prefer stationary high fidelity speakers over automotive control devices.
Luxury car owners already have advanced built in media displays integrated into dashboards.

questions.caseTitle: Bonus: Launching Netflix ad supported subscription tier
questions.scenario: Netflix is launching a lower priced subscription tier that includes commercial advertisements.
questions.question: Who is the primary target segment for this new ad supported plan?
options: Traditional cable television subscribers who never use streaming
Hardcore binge watchers who hate any commercial interruptions
Price sensitive streamers who previously shared passwords
Wealthy families who buy every premium streaming service
questions.explanation: Price sensitive users and former password sharers who find standard tiers too expensive are the ideal audience. They are willing to watch ads in exchange for a lower monthly price.
whyWrong: Traditional cable subscribers who avoid streaming require different acquisition channels.
Hardcore binge watchers explicitly pay top dollar to avoid commercial interruptions entirely.
Wealthy families typically upgrade to ad free plans for uninterrupted viewing experiences.

positioning.subtitle: Crafting a differentiated value proposition for your chosen segment.

lesson.hook: Stop selling features everyone has and start owning the reason you matter.
lesson.what: Positioning defines how your product stands apart from competitors in the mind of your target user. It connects your unique strengths directly to the specific problems your chosen segment cares about most.
how: Identify the primary competitor your segment currently uses today.
Pinpoint the single major capability they completely lack.
Claim that exact capability as your core differentiator.
lesson.example: Zoom entering team messaging by weaponizing live meetings instead of outslacking Slack. They targeted users drowning in app switches with in-meeting chat continuity.
lesson.mistake: Trying to appeal to everyone by listing generic benefits instead of taking a hard stand against existing alternatives.

questions.caseTitle: How would you position a new AI writing tool against Microsoft?
questions.scenario: Microsoft has Copilot baked into Word and Google has Duet in Docs. Fighting them on convenience or broad spelling checks is impossible.
questions.question: How should you position your new AI writing tool against these giants?
options: Highlight our superior spelling correction speed across all standard desktop web browsers.
Focus on offering lower monthly pricing plans for casual everyday student users.
Market our product as the easiest artificial intelligence assistant for writing emails.
Target professional copywriters by emphasizing deep brand voice customization.
questions.explanation: You must avoid direct feature parity with platform giants and instead target a specialized workflow need. Professional copywriters require advanced voice control that generic office assistants completely miss.
whyWrong: Speed and spelling are core features already commoditized by Microsoft and Google directly inside documents.
Lower pricing fails because students have zero willingness to pay when free tools exist.
Email writing is a broad use case where giant office suites naturally dominate through sheer convenience.

questions.caseTitle: How would Microsoft Teams enter the education market against Google Classroom?
questions.scenario: Google Classroom owns primary and secondary schools because it runs inside free Gmail accounts and Chromebooks.
questions.question: What positioning angle should Microsoft Teams take to carve out a winning market share?
options: Emphasize simpler interface designs for young students using cheap classroom tablet devices.
Provide faster assignment grading tools for elementary school teachers working late nights.
Target higher education departments needing complex research collaboration and enterprise IT security.
Offer lower subscription costs for cash strapped primary and secondary school district buyers.
questions.explanation: Microsoft cannot out-give free tools in primary schools, so positioning must shift to higher education. Universities require security and research tools that basic free platforms fail to provide.
whyWrong: Simple tablet interfaces play directly into Google Classroom and Chromebook core strengths.
Elementary school teachers lack budget authority and primarily rely on district mandated tools.
Competing on price against a completely free product in primary schools is a losing battle.

questions.caseTitle: Competitive Positioning and Differentiation
questions.scenario: You need to enter team messaging not by out-slacking Slack, but by leveraging an unfair advantage.
questions.question: How should Zoom position its new team messaging product to win market share?
options: Weaponize the live meeting by turning calls instantly into permanent threaded workspace discussions.
Promote faster message delivery speeds across global mobile device operating networks.
Focus entirely on offering cheaper subscription plans for cash strapped startup company teams.
Highlight superior file storage capacity compared to legacy communication software platforms.
questions.explanation: Zoom already owns the live meeting, making it the natural wedge to anchor ongoing team discussions. Positioning around meeting context solves the fatigue of switching between apps.
whyWrong: Message delivery speed is technically expected and rarely drives a major platform switch.
Competing on low price alone attracts low value customers without building sustainable habits.
File storage is a commoditized utility feature that fails to create a strong emotional wedge.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch a premium subscription tier for Spotify?
questions.scenario: Spotify wants to capture revenue from hardcore audiophiles and high income households without breaking the core model.
questions.question: How should Spotify position this new HiFi premium tier to attract the right users?
options: Market it as the best way to discover trending viral pop tracks with friends.
Position it around lossless studio quality audio for dedicated music enthusiasts and gear owners.
Focus on delivering faster playlist generation speeds using advanced machine learning models.
Promote it as a cheaper alternative for families sharing single household accounts together.
questions.explanation: Hardcore audiophiles care deeply about sound fidelity above all else, making studio quality the core wedge. This justifies a higher price point without cannibalizing the standard tier.
whyWrong: Viral pop discovery is already solved perfectly well by the standard ad supported and premium tiers.
Playlist generation speed is an invisible background metric rather than a distinct premium benefit.
Positioning a premium tier as a cheaper option undermines the entire value capture strategy.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Shopify's point-of-sale system to small retailers.
questions.scenario: You are launching Shopify point-of-sale hardware to small retailers who currently operate online stores.
questions.question: What is the most effective positioning angle for targeting these existing digital merchants?
options: Position it as the ultimate bridge unifying their online catalog with pop up shop inventory.
Highlight the lowest hardware manufacturing costs compared to traditional payment processing terminals.
Focus on providing advanced employee shift scheduling tools for busy physical retail locations.
Market the sleek aesthetic design of the card reader for trendy boutique store owners.
questions.explanation: Online merchants running weekend pop ups suffer from inventory sync nightmares between digital and physical sales. Positioning around unified inventory directly solves their most painful operational headache.
whyWrong: Competing solely on hardware manufacturing cost invites a destructive race to the bottom.
Employee scheduling is an HR problem, not the core commerce synchronization challenge.
Aesthetic design matters, but operational inventory sync drives the actual business decision.

questions.caseTitle: Design a GTM strategy for a fintech app in low connectivity areas.
questions.scenario: You are launching a fintech app in semi rural regions with erratic internet and low smartphone penetration.
questions.question: How should you position your product offering for micro merchants in these specific markets?
options: Position it as a reliable offline ledger that syncs transactions automatically when connection returns.
Promote lightning fast international wire transfer speeds for global digital nomad freelancers.
Highlight advanced investment portfolio management tools for high yield cryptocurrency trading strategies.
Market the application as a seamless replacement for traditional desktop banking software platforms.
questions.explanation: Micro merchants in low connectivity areas struggle daily with dropped signals and lost transaction records. Positioning around robust offline reliability directly addresses their primary operational fear.
whyWrong: International wire transfers miss the local trade and cash flow needs of market stall vendors.
Cryptocurrency trading is completely irrelevant to daily cash flow management for market stall vendors.
Desktop banking software does not apply to semi rural kiosk operators without personal computers.

questions.caseTitle: Bonus: Launching Netflix Cloud Gaming
questions.scenario: Netflix is launching a cloud gaming service bundled directly into existing television and mobile streaming apps.
questions.question: How should Netflix position this new gaming offering to its massive existing subscriber base?
options: Focus on offering lower subscription fees than standalone gaming services in the market.
Position it as zero friction gaming with no extra downloads required on your current TV.
Market the service as a complete replacement for high end dedicated console hardware.
Highlight hardcore competitive multiplayer esports matchmaking for professional gaming enthusiasts.
questions.explanation: Netflix's biggest unfair advantage is that users are already logged in and holding a streaming remote. Positioning around instant play without downloads removes the friction that kills casual gaming adoption.
whyWrong: Discounting the bundle fails to leverage the unique convenience of the existing Netflix app.
Replacing dedicated consoles alienates core gamers and overpromises on casual capabilities.
Hardcore esports players demand high end hardware and low latency setups that streaming cannot match.

questions.caseTitle: Bonus: Launching Slack Canvas for Enterprise
questions.scenario: Slack is launching Canvas to give teams a persistent space for notes alongside their fast moving chat channels.
questions.question: What positioning angle should Slack use to differentiate Canvas from standard wiki documents?
options: Emphasize superior typography formatting controls for professional technical writers and journalists.
Highlight faster PDF export capabilities for sharing formal business reports with external clients.
Market the product as the cheapest standalone document editing software for enterprise companies.
Position it as living project workspace where chat discussions instantly become permanent team records.
questions.explanation: Traditional wikis like Notion or Confluence suffer from low engagement because they sit outside daily communication. Positioning Canvas as the bridge where ephemeral chat turns into permanent knowledge solves context loss.
whyWrong: Technical writers and journalists use dedicated publishing tools rather than team chat software.
PDF exports are a minor utility feature that fails to capture the core collaborative workflow.
Positioning as a cheap standalone editor forces a brutal head to head fight against entrenched docs.

pricing_and_packaging.subtitle: Master pricing tied to real value and willingness to pay

lesson.hook: Stop guessing numbers on a napkin and start pricing based on actual delivered value.
lesson.what: Pricing and packaging determine how you capture value from your target segment. You must align cost structures with customer willingness to pay rather than random guessing.
how: Identify the core value metric customers care about most.
Analyze competitor pricing tiers and customer willingness to pay.
Structure packaging to naturally upsell users as usage scales.
lesson.example: For Spotify HiFi, we tie premium pricing directly to audiophile sound quality and high disposable income. This ensures the tier captures maximum revenue without cannibalizing the ad-supported base.
lesson.mistake: Copying competitor pricing models without validating whether your beachhead segment shares the same willingness to pay.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch a premium subscription tier for Spotify?
questions.scenario: Spotify is designing the HiFi tier for audiophiles and high-income households who want lossless streaming.
questions.question: How should Spotify structure the pricing and packaging for this new tier?
options: Offer it free initially to drive massive early adoption numbers.
Bundle it with all existing podcast ads for maximum confusion.
Price it strictly based on competitor audio service monthly fees.
Charge a modest markup tied directly to audio quality improvements.
questions.explanation: Tying the markup to the specific value delivered ensures audiophiles feel the price is fair. It protects core margins while capturing surplus from high-income users.
whyWrong: Giving it away free fails to monetize the distinct willingness to pay of audiophiles.
Bundling with ads confuses the core value proposition of a premium audio tier.
Pricing purely off competitors ignores your unique cost structure and willingness to pay.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Adobe Creative Cloud's student plan in smaller cities.
questions.scenario: Adobe wants to acquire students in smaller Indian cities where piracy is rampant and willingness to pay is near zero.
questions.question: What pricing strategy should Adobe deploy to convert these students?
options: Introduce hyper-localized micro pricing aligned with local student budgets.
Require annual upfront payments to filter out low-income users.
Maintain global pricing to protect premium brand perception everywhere.
Double prices to signal superior software quality over pirated tools.
questions.explanation: Localized pricing matches the stark reality of lower purchasing power in tier two cities. This undercuts piracy by making legal access affordable.
whyWrong: Requiring annual upfront payments creates an insurmountable barrier for budget students.
Maintaining global pricing ensures continuous high piracy rates in low-income regions.
Raising prices further drives students directly toward free pirated alternatives.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Shopify's point-of-sale system to small retailers.
questions.scenario: Shopify is targeting online merchants who also run physical weekend pop-up shops or small boutiques.
questions.question: How should Shopify package and price this new point-of-sale hardware and software?
options: Force merchants to buy expensive dedicated hardware bundles upfront immediately.
Charge a massive enterprise implementation fee for each pop-up shop.
Bundle software access directly into existing online store subscription plans.
Offer software completely free while taking zero transaction fee revenue.
questions.explanation: Bundling the POS software into existing plans removes friction for current online merchants. It leverages their existing subscription to drive offline adoption.
whyWrong: Forcing expensive upfront hardware purchases creates friction for casual weekend merchants.
Enterprise implementation fees will instantly scare away small weekend pop-up boutique owners.
Zero transaction fees and free software leaves no viable path to monetization.

questions.caseTitle: How would you position a new AI writing tool against Microsoft?
questions.scenario: A startup is launching an AI writing tool targeting professional copywriters and agency content leads.
questions.question: What is the optimal pricing and packaging model for this professional segment?
options: Charge per seat with unlimited generations for large enterprise teams.
Charge purely per word generated to penalize long-form agency writers.
Match Microsoft Copilot exact pricing to avoid losing budget battles.
Tier pricing based on advanced brand voice training and collaborative workflows.
questions.explanation: Professional copywriters value advanced brand voice customization and team workflows. Pricing based on these specific capabilities captures their higher willingness to pay.
whyWrong: Unlimited generations can destroy margins due to high underlying model inference costs.
Charging per word penalizes long-form copywriters and discourages heavy platform usage.
Matching tech giants directly leads to a brutal pricing war you cannot win.

questions.caseTitle: Design a GTM strategy for a fintech app in low connectivity areas.
questions.scenario: A fintech app is expanding into semi-rural East Africa targeting micro-merchants running market stalls.
questions.question: How should the product be packaged and priced for these low-income micro-merchants?
options: Implement heavy monthly subscription fees for basic digital wallet access.
Require minimum account balances that exclude casual daily market traders.
Package features into complex tiers requiring high data connectivity.
Charge transaction fees per transfer with zero upfront monthly costs.
questions.explanation: Micro-merchants have fluctuating daily cash flows and cannot afford fixed monthly fees. Pay-per-transaction aligns costs directly with their revenue generation.
whyWrong: Monthly subscription fees will cause merchants to abandon the app for cash.
Minimum account balances will immediately exclude the poorest market stall vendors.
Complex tiers require data connectivity that these semi-rural regions lack entirely.

questions.caseTitle: Pricing Strategy and GTM Alignment
questions.scenario: Uber is launching a premium tier for corporate accounts needing centralized expense controls and executive pickups.
questions.question: How should Uber price and package this B2B corporate offering?
options: Charge a flat monthly platform fee per company plus standard ride fares.
Price per individual employee signup regardless of active ride usage.
Copy consumer surge pricing models without any corporate billing controls.
Offer free rides to all employees until company executives demand upgrades.
questions.explanation: A flat platform fee combined with standard ride fares captures software value while monetizing utilization. It fits corporate procurement expectations perfectly.
whyWrong: Pricing per employee signup ignores the reality that many staff members rarely travel.
Copying pure consumer models ignores the core corporate need for centralized billing.
Offering free rides indefinitely creates unsustainable burn without validating corporate budget.

questions.caseTitle: Notion Team Workspace Launch
questions.scenario: Notion is launching a new enterprise collaboration tier for fast-growing tech startups with remote teams.
questions.question: What pricing metric best captures willingness to pay for this workspace tool?
options: Charge flat fees per company regardless of total active team size.
Offer all collaboration features free and monetize via banner advertisements.
Price based on active collaborating members and advanced security controls.
Charge per gigabyte of uploaded document storage used by engineers.
questions.explanation: Pricing per active member scales naturally as companies grow, while gating security features captures enterprise willingness to pay.
whyWrong: Flat company fees fail to capture revenue expansion as startups rapidly hire.
Banner advertisements destroy the professional focus required in a collaboration tool.
Charging by storage penalizes documentation heavy teams and drives them away.

questions.caseTitle: Stripe Invoicing Expansion
questions.scenario: Stripe is introducing an advanced automated invoicing tier for scaling B2B SaaS companies.
questions.question: How should Stripe structure the pricing for this new automated billing tier?
options: Price based on the total number of customer support tickets resolved.
Provide unlimited free processing while charging for basic PDF downloads.
Take a small percentage fee of total invoice volume processed successfully.
Charge massive fixed setup fees before allowing any invoice creation.
questions.explanation: A percentage of invoice volume aligns Stripe revenue directly with the financial growth of the B2B SaaS customer.
whyWrong: Support tickets have no correlation to the financial value of automated invoicing.
Charging for basic PDF downloads while processing volume for free makes no sense.
Fixed setup fees create high friction and slow down initial product adoption rates.

launch_metrics.subtitle: Define launch goals and clear success thresholds

lesson.hook: Numbers or it did not happen on launch day.
lesson.what: Launch metrics define what success looks like with hard numbers. They prevent moving goalposts after your product goes live.
how: Pick one primary north star metric for the launch window.
Set a clear timebound target like ninety days.
Define guardrail metrics to monitor negative side effects.
lesson.example: For Spotify HiFi, aiming for ten percent conversion in twelve months while keeping churn below two percent.
lesson.mistake: Setting vague goals like increasing user engagement without specifying any concrete numbers.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch a premium subscription tier for Spotify?
questions.scenario: Spotify is introducing the new HiFi tier for hardcore audiophiles to drive incremental revenue.
questions.question: What is the best primary launch metric for this subscription tier?
options: Reaching fifty million total free tier users over the first six months.
Achieving ten percent conversion of existing premium subscribers within twelve months.
Generating five hundred thousand social media impressions in the first month.
Getting two thousand user reviews on the app store within ninety days.
questions.explanation: This metric directly measures monetization of the target audience within a defined timeframe. It ties revenue goals to actual user adoption.
whyWrong: Free tier users do not generate subscription revenue for a premium tier.
Social media impressions do not reflect actual paid conversion or revenue.
App store reviews measure sentiment rather than business model success.

questions.caseTitle: Design a launch plan for a D2C brand entering a new market.
questions.scenario: Quince is expanding its affordable cashmere brand into the British market with a tight beachhead.
questions.question: What is the best primary success metric for this international market entry?
options: Reaching one million pounds in net revenue within the first ninety days.
Gaining five million organic website visitors globally during the first year.
Signing up ten thousand newsletter subscribers across every European country.
Securing three celebrity endorsements on Instagram within thirty days.
questions.explanation: Net revenue within a specific timeframe proves market demand and commercial viability. It keeps the team focused on financial results.
whyWrong: Global website visitors is too broad for a focused British market entry.
Newsletter subscribers across Europe violate the targeted beachhead strategy.
Celebrity endorsements are marketing tactics rather than core business goals.

questions.caseTitle: Plan the launch of a B2B SaaS product for small businesses.
questions.scenario: A new B2B SaaS product is targeting small retail shops with zero dedicated IT staff.
questions.question: Which combination of launch metrics best defines success for this product?
options: Five million total page views on our marketing blog in the first year.
One thousand active paying customers within ninety days with low acquisition costs.
Two hundred thousand free trials started without checking any payment details.
Fifty enterprise partnerships signed with major global retail conglomerates quickly.
questions.explanation: Paying customers and acquisition costs measure both demand and unit economics. This proves the small business model is sustainable.
whyWrong: Page views measure content traffic rather than software sales or usage.
Free trials without payment info do not validate actual willingness to pay.
Enterprise conglomerates contradict the small retail shop target segment.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch Amazon's same-day delivery in a new city?
questions.scenario: Amazon is launching same-day delivery in Atlanta while managing driver network density constraints.
questions.question: What primary metrics should define the success of this city launch?
options: Signing up every single local retail merchant within the first six weeks.
Zero customer support tickets regarding late deliveries during week one.
Reaching ten million total platform orders globally in the first year.
One hundred thousand active users in ninety days with high on-time delivery rates.
questions.explanation: Tracking active users alongside on-time delivery balances growth with operational reliability. It ensures quality matches demand.
whyWrong: Signing every merchant is an unrealistic goal that ignores market realities.
Zero support tickets is an impossible operational standard for any launch.
Global orders do not measure the specific performance of the Atlanta launch.

questions.caseTitle: Design the GTM for Meta's WhatsApp Business API in Europe.
questions.scenario: Meta is launching the WhatsApp Business API for European small and medium businesses.
questions.question: What are the most appropriate launch metrics for this business API?
options: Five million consumer messages sent through the platform on day one.
One hundred thousand active accounts with retention above sixty percent after three months.
Twenty million dollars spent on television advertising across all European regions.
Ten thousand press articles published about the product in major newspapers.
questions.explanation: Active accounts combined with medium-term retention prove real business utility. It shows merchants find ongoing value in the tool.
whyWrong: Consumer messages do not track whether businesses are adopting the tool.
Television advertising spend is an input metric rather than a business result.
Press articles measure media coverage rather than product adoption.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Shopify's point-of-sale system to small retailers.
questions.scenario: Shopify is launching its point-of-sale hardware to online merchants who also run weekend pop-up stores.
questions.question: What is the best primary launch metric for this new hardware offering?
options: One million retail shoppers tapping their credit cards on day one globally.
Achieving zero hardware manufacturing defects across the initial supplier batch.
Fifty thousand existing online merchants processing offline sales within six months.
Selling five hundred thousand point-of-sale devices to completely offline mom and pops.
questions.explanation: Leveraging existing online merchants directly targets the defined beachhead segment. It measures cross-sell success effectively.
whyWrong: Shopper taps depend on consumer traffic rather than merchant platform adoption.
Manufacturing defects are a supply chain check rather than a GTM success metric.
Selling to offline stores violates the strategy of targeting existing online merchants.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Notion AI to Personal and Team Users
questions.scenario: Notion is launching a new generative AI writing assistant to its existing base of productivity workspace users.
questions.question: What is the most effective launch metric for this new AI feature?
options: Five hundred thousand dollars spent on billboard advertisements in major cities.
Zero server downtime during the first week of public feature availability.
Ten million new signups from people who have never used Notion before.
Twenty percent of active workspaces using the AI tool weekly within sixty days.
questions.explanation: Weekly workspace adoption measures real product utility among existing users. It avoids vanity metrics and focuses on habit formation.
whyWrong: Billboard spend is an input metric that does not indicate product value.
Server uptime is an engineering reliability metric rather than a GTM goal.
New signups measure top of funnel acquisition rather than feature adoption.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Apple Fitness Plus in New Global Markets
questions.scenario: Apple is expanding its subscription fitness service into five new international markets with localized content.
questions.question: Which metric best indicates a successful international market launch?
options: Winning three major design awards for the application interface.
Producing five hundred hours of workout video content locally.
Getting two million free trial downloads in the very first weekend.
Reaching fifty thousand paid subscribers per new market within six months.
questions.explanation: Paid subscribers per market directly measures commercial success and market fit. It proves users are willing to pay for the localized service.
whyWrong: Design awards reflect aesthetic quality rather than business launch success.
Workout hours produced measure content output rather than customer adoption.
Free trial downloads do not guarantee long-term retention or paid conversion.

channel_strategy.subtitle: Match your distribution channels to where your customers actually are.

lesson.hook: Stop buying billboards when your users live exclusively inside developer Slack channels.
lesson.what: Channel strategy ensures you reach your target segment efficiently. You must pick distribution paths that fit their daily habits.
how: Find where your specific audience hangs out
Calculate acquisition costs for each potential path
Prioritize high-leverage channels over broad advertising
lesson.example: For Shopify POS, we leverage existing merchant digital dashboards rather than chasing offline boutiques. This completely eliminates expensive cold outreach overhead.
lesson.mistake: Picking channels based on vanity metrics instead of sustainable unit economics.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Shopify's point-of-sale system to small retailers.
questions.scenario: Shopify is launching a new physical point of sale hardware system for independent retail store owners.
questions.question: Which distribution channel best minimizes early acquisition costs for this hardware rollout?
options: Target existing online Shopify merchants running weekend pop up boutiques.
Hire door to door sales teams for every local main street.
Launch national television advertising campaigns during prime evening time slots.
Partner with massive enterprise department store chains across the country.
questions.explanation: Existing digital merchants already trust Shopify and represent a captive, low friction audience. Targeting them avoids the extreme costs of acquiring completely offline mom and pop shops.
whyWrong: Door to door sales teams have massive overhead and terrible unit economics for hardware.
Mass market television is far too expensive and misses the targeted merchant demographic.
Enterprise department stores have long sales cycles and completely different operational needs.

questions.caseTitle: How would Microsoft Teams enter the education market against Google Classroom?
questions.scenario: Microsoft Teams wants to capture market share in education against entrenched Google Classroom users.
questions.question: Which channel strategy should Microsoft use to bypass Google dominance in primary schools?
options: Focus exclusively on higher education departments requiring complex research collaboration features.
Partner with consumer hardware manufacturers to preinstall desktop software icons.
Buy sponsored ads across every major social media platform for teachers.
Send physical flyers to every single household in the school district.
questions.explanation: Google dominates primary education through free Gmail accounts, so Microsoft must target universities where advanced security matters more. This avoids fighting an unwinnable channel war in elementary schools.
whyWrong: Preinstalling desktop icons on consumer hardware fails to reach institutional IT decision makers.
Social media ads targeting teachers have low conversion rates for enterprise education tools.
Physical flyers are extremely expensive and poorly targeted for software purchasing decisions.

questions.caseTitle: Launch Tesla's electric vehicles in India.
questions.scenario: Tesla is planning its market entry into India under heavy import tariffs and zero charging infrastructure.
questions.question: How should Tesla structure its initial distribution and sales channel in this market?
options: Partner with local grocery delivery services for vehicle drop offs.
Build massive dealership networks across every rural village immediately.
Rely entirely on online drop shipping without any physical presence.
Target wealthiest urban pockets directly through flagship experience stores.
questions.explanation: Flagship stores in wealthy urban centers match the initial charging density and high income segment. Mass market distribution would fail due to severe infrastructure constraints outside major cities.
whyWrong: Grocery delivery services lack the capability to handle high value automotive logistics.
Rural villages lack charging density and have zero purchasing power for luxury cars.
Online drop shipping is impossible for physical luxury vehicles requiring test drives.

questions.caseTitle: Design the GTM for Meta's WhatsApp Business API in Europe.
questions.scenario: Meta is launching the WhatsApp Business API across Europe for small and medium merchants.
questions.question: Which channel approach is most effective for reaching resource constrained merchants at scale?
options: Distribute printed brochures through traditional postal mail campaigns.
Open luxury retail storefronts in major capital European cities.
Sponsor international Formula One racing teams for brand awareness.
Integrate directly with regional point of sale software platforms they already use.
questions.explanation: Integrating with existing software platforms places the API where merchants already manage operations. This drastically lowers acquisition friction compared to traditional outbound sales.
whyWrong: Postal mail is slow, expensive, and easily ignored by busy small business owners.
Luxury storefronts make no sense for digital software APIs targeting small merchants.
Formula One sponsorships build general consumer awareness rather than business API adoption.

questions.caseTitle: Design a GTM strategy for a fintech app in low connectivity areas.
questions.scenario: A fintech startup is launching a financial app for micro merchants in low connectivity East African regions.
questions.question: What primary distribution channel bypasses standard app store and internet limitations here?
options: Partner with local market stall associations and mobile money agents.
Run high budget digital banner ads on global tech websites.
Broadcast national radio advertisements during peak morning commute hours.
Publish lengthy whitepapers on academic financial research journals.
questions.explanation: Partnering with trusted local agents and market associations leverages existing human networks. This solves the trust and connectivity barriers that prevent standard app store downloads.
whyWrong: Global tech websites target users with reliable internet, completely missing this demographic.
Radio ads raise general awareness but fail to drive direct app activation or trust.
Academic whitepapers are irrelevant to micro merchants running local market stalls.

questions.caseTitle: How would you launch a premium subscription tier for Spotify?
questions.scenario: Spotify is introducing a new high fidelity audio subscription tier for audiophiles and affluent households.
questions.question: Which initial channel should Spotify use to drive the highest conversion of this new tier?
options: Sponsor billboard posters along major highway commuting corridors.
Promote directly inside the core app to existing premium subscribers.
Place cold outbound sales calls to random free tier listeners.
Distribute physical compact discs through traditional record store chains.
questions.explanation: Existing premium subscribers are already paying and have proven musical engagement. Targeting them inside the app yields the highest conversion with almost zero extra marketing cost.
whyWrong: Highway billboards lack precise segmentation for high end audio streaming features.
Cold outbound calls to free tier users are expensive and annoy potential customers.
Compact discs are obsolete for a streaming platform launching a digital audio tier.

questions.caseTitle: Bonus Case: Notion AI Launch
questions.scenario: Notion is launching a new standalone AI note taking companion for existing workspace power users.
questions.question: What is the most cost effective channel to drive initial adoption of this feature?
options: Insert contextual upgrade prompts directly inside existing workspace pages.
Hire external telemarketing agencies to cold call enterprise executives.
Purchase expensive national television commercial spots during sports broadcasts.
Mail printed product manuals to every university campus library.
questions.explanation: Contextual in app prompts reach users exactly when they are creating documents, maximizing relevance. This leverages the existing product surface area instead of paying for external acquisition.
whyWrong: Telemarketing is highly inefficient and universally disliked by modern enterprise buyers.
Television commercials are far too broad and expensive for a niche productivity tool.
Printed manuals are useless for fast moving digital software products and features.

questions.caseTitle: Bonus Case: Figma Dev Mode
questions.scenario: Figma is launching Dev Mode to bridge the workflow gap between product designers and software engineers.
questions.question: Which adoption channel ensures rapid penetration within software engineering teams?
options: Run paid banner advertisements on popular fashion and lifestyle blogs.
Distribute promotional flyers at international automotive trade shows.
Embed invitations directly inside existing design files shared with developers.
Set up physical demonstration booths at local farmers markets.
questions.explanation: Embedding invitations where designers already collaborate with engineers creates natural viral loops. Engineers naturally encounter the tool when inspecting design files for their daily work.
whyWrong: Fashion and lifestyle blogs have zero overlap with professional software engineers.
Automotive trade shows miss the core audience of digital product development teams.
Farmers markets are completely unrelated to technical software development workflows.
